common_name: New York Improved Eggplant (New York Spineless)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost date and hold seedlings under warm, bright conditions until the soil has warmed thoroughly.

directions: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost, keeping the soil warm since eggplant germinates poorly below 70F, then transplant out only after nights stay reliably warm. Give plants full sun, even moisture, and a stake or cage to support the heavy fruit load once pods set. This is one of the oldest American commercial eggplant selections, dating to the late 1800s, prized for its large glossy purple-black fruit and mild, tender flesh, and it stands as a direct ancestor of many modern hybrids sold today. Because it lacks the disease tolerance bred into newer types, gardeners often see best results with crop rotation and floating row cover early in the season.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost date and transplant once the soil is consistently warm and nights are frost-free.

directions: Sow indoors under warm conditions and transplant into rich, well-drained soil once temperatures are reliably warm, since this heirloom is sensitive to cold snaps. Space plants generously and water evenly to keep the slender fruit from developing a bitter edge. Early Long Purple is a traditional Italian variety valued for producing its slim, curved, deep-purple fruit earlier than many other eggplant types, making it a useful choice for gardeners in shorter-season regions. Its thin skin and few seeds make it popular for frying and grilling whole.

subcategory: small round black-purple Middle Eastern heirloom eggplant

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost date, providing consistent bottom heat, then transplant into hot, sunny beds after frost danger has passed.

directions: Start seed indoors with steady warmth and transplant into full sun after the soil has warmed, since this heirloom thrives in hot climates and resents cool, wet soil. Keep watering consistent to avoid stress that can toughen the skin. Aswad, whose name means "black" in Arabic, is an Iraqi heirloom prized for its small, round, near-black fruit and dense, creamy flesh that holds up well in stews and grilling. It is a favorite among growers seeking heat-tolerant regional varieties adapted to arid conditions.

subcategory: large green-striped South Indian heirloom eggplant

directions: Sow indoors and transplant into full sun once the weather is reliably warm, giving plants sturdy stakes since the fruit can grow quite large and heavy. Regular, deep watering helps produce tender, sweet flesh. Udumalapet takes its name from a town in Tamil Nadu, India, and is grown for its large, rounded fruit with pale green skin marked by faint white striping. Home cooks favor it for curries and roasting because of its mild flavor and relatively few seeds.

subcategory: Italian-type hybrid eggplant bred for productivity

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost date and transplant after the soil has warmed and frost danger has passed.

directions: Start seed indoors under warm conditions and transplant into fertile, well-drained soil once nights stay above 55F, since this hybrid performs best with steady heat. Provide even moisture and support for the upright plants as fruit clusters develop. Antigua is a modern Italian-type hybrid bred for a compact plant habit and heavy early set of glossy, dark purple, oval fruit, making it a reliable choice for market growers and small gardens alike. Its relatively quick maturity suits gardeners in cooler regions who want classic eggplant flavor without a long growing season.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost date and set out transplants once the soil is warm and nights are frost-free.

directions: Sow indoors with warm soil temperatures and transplant into full sun after frost danger has passed, keeping plants evenly watered so the tender skin does not toughen. Mulching helps retain the consistent moisture this heirloom prefers. Beatrice is an Italian heirloom similar in type to Rosa Bianca, producing rounded to oval fruit blushed rose-pink over creamy white, with dense, mild, and notably low-bitterness flesh. It is often grown for its striking market appearance as well as its tender texture when roasted or grilled.

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost date and transplant into containers or garden beds once the weather is reliably warm.

directions: Start seed indoors and transplant into a sunny spot or a large container after the last frost, keeping the compact plants consistently watered since their smaller root systems dry out faster than standard eggplant. Deadheading spent fruit encourages continued production through the season. Slim Jim produces slender, finger-sized purple fruit on a small, bushy plant, making it a popular choice for patio containers and small gardens where space is limited. Its petite size and attractive purple flowers also make it a common pick for ornamental-edible plantings.

planting.note: Direct sow 1-3 weeks after the last frost once the soil has warmed, since okra seedlings resent cold, wet soil and transplant poorly.

directions: Direct sow after the soil has warmed and all frost danger has passed, soaking seed overnight to speed germination, then thin seedlings to allow room for these towering plants to spread. Harvest curved pods every day or two while young and tender, since they toughen quickly once mature. Fife Creek Cowhorn is a Southern heirloom known for its exceptionally tall growth, often reaching well over six feet, and its long, curved, rib-free pods reminiscent of a cow's horn. Gardeners who grow it out for seed appreciate its reliable productivity in hot, humid summers.

planting.note: Direct sow 1-3 weeks after the last frost once soil temperatures are consistently warm, soaking seed beforehand to improve germination.

directions: Sow directly into warm garden soil after frost danger has passed, since okra grows poorly if started indoors and transplanted. Pick the deep red pods small and often to keep plants productive through the heat of summer. Bowling Red is a Kentucky heirloom valued for its striking burgundy-red pods and reddish stems, which add ornamental interest to the vegetable garden as well as color to the harvest basket. The pods darken to a rich maroon-green when cooked but retain their tender texture if picked young.

planting.note: Direct sow 1-3 weeks after the last frost once the soil is warm, spacing seed to allow the compact bushy plants room to branch.

directions: Direct sow into warm soil after the last frost, soaking seed overnight to promote even germination, then thin to give plants adequate spacing for good air circulation. Harvest the ribbed, tapering pods young and often to keep the compact plants producing steadily. Dwarf Green Long Pod is a long-standing heirloom selected for its shorter, bushier habit compared to older tall okra types, making it easier to harvest while still delivering abundant, tender green pods. Its manageable size has kept it a staple in home gardens with limited space.

planting.note: Direct sow 1-3 weeks after the last frost once the soil has warmed to at least 65F, since cold soil causes poor, uneven germination.

Pick pods every day or two once they begin forming, since Green Velvet quickly grows past its tender stage. This long-cultivated variety produces smooth, spineless, dark green pods on a vigorous, productive plant, and it has been a dependable garden staple for generations of Southern cooks who value its mild flavor in gumbo and frying. Its smooth pod surface also makes it easier to handle at harvest than spinier heirloom types.
